channel.title: What changed · Amal Mehta
channel.description: What changed on amalmehta.com, day by day.

item.title: Site changes, November 27, 2026
item.description: Travel: pressing a place's drawing, or the map button in its corner, swaps it for a zoomed-in patch of the world map with that place's pin pulsing. The place cards sit on soft panels with more room between rows. The Matrix joins Films I love. Faouzia and Hans Zimmer each get a line.

item.title: Site changes, November 26, 2026
item.description: The hero names the Redwood Center's Sensorimotor AI journal club. Open to links the questions I can't let go of. The robot soccer entry gets a Try it live link that opens its simulation in place. Interests' Now lists the two papers I'm reading. Death Valley moves to Places I've been. Outside work's races read in order. The BCI card says what was simulated in plain words. Volcán Chimborazo joins Places I'd like to go with its own drawing and map pin. Neuro Falcon gets its own deep dive. The thesis PDF gets a cover page. Skills chips find the work that used them. The Rewarding deep dive and the BCI line match their cards. Link previews are retaken. An unused 85 KB font is gone. What changed splits each change into lines, links each day's dot and gets its own RSS feed. The iPhone apps link to their entries. The Drone Autonomy card gets an ink margin note, the iPhone apps show live glimpses, What changed opens with an eight-week activity strip, and the footer credits rise into place on every page. Deep dives light up their method steps, show a year line of related work and link each part. The tab icon follows the sky. A What changed page replaces the GitHub link. Link previews and the search snippet are current. Publication lines link to their entries. IPhone apps are listed as coming soon. Publications gets the filling rail, Neuro Falcon gets a sketch of a decoder drifting and recovering, the games show live previews on hover, and Acatenango joins Places I'd like to go with its own drawing and map pin. Neuro Falcon joins More projects, Outside work lists the games, the phone header no longer overlaps, the BCI label is shorter, and Skills matches current work (adds Hugging Face Transformers, scikit-learn, React and LLM agents. Stable-baselines3 saved for later). Featured cards line up (titles, tags and links level, Drone Autonomy spans the row on the same columns), and the deep-dive nav keeps Back to the profile centred. Drone Autonomy is back in Featured, the BCI card gets a shorter line and a live replay of its day-by-day results, the INFORMS 2021 poster joins Publications, and the SPIE papers get a Cite button. Publications & reports adds the Stanford AA273 pose graph optimization report, with a sketch of a drifting path snapping into a closed loop. Publications & reports adds the 2016 WaferSat spacecraft paper from SPIE, with a sketch of a laser pushing a tiny sail. The header carries a sun or moon for the visitor's local time, Thinking shows how many days each question has been open, and deep dives end with a next-project card and have figures that zoom full screen.

item.title: Site changes, November 25, 2026
item.description: Each publication gets a tiny moving sketch, the Open to lines light up one by one, and Kilimanjaro and the 130-foot dives show a climb and a depth gauge on hover. Publications & reports adds the robot soccer thesis, the USCAP 2022 abstract, and the CS330 and CS285 class reports. The jet and soccer sims open from small faint icons in their drawings' corners, the soccer and drone deep dives open their sims in place, app screenshots play a live glimpse, and Writings keeps the paragraph you're reading in full ink. The PhysicsAI drawing opens into a fighter-jet flight sim over a mountain island: fly it or hand it to an autopilot that works out a damaged or loaded jet in a few seconds and flies the gates. The robot soccer drawing opens into a live 3D pitch where the policy reaches, kicks and waits, or you drive, with sliders for ball, grass, wind and sensor noise. AlphaGo Lite is back in More projects and plays in its card. The Now chip turns over between what's current, earlier research gets a flaring supernova and spraying particle tracks, and the header settles once you scroll. Research & work ends with earlier research: supernovae with the Perlmutter Cosmology Group and particle interactions at the Berkeley Institute for Data Science. A pen flourish signs under the name after the intro, the belief tabs wipe in, A hard day's rainbow develops into colour, the 404 drawing twinkles and its trail wanders, and Thinking's line runs beside the numbers instead of through them. The unwritten education question rests until it has its words, the tools question gets its bet, and Theory of AGI becomes a question like the rest. The contour lines behind Outside work and Endurance drift toward the cursor, and the Scuba diving, Skiing and Photography tiles bubble, snow and flash. The title matches the hero again, the hero says it in one sentence, the flagship's label says what the 50 experiments were, Now reads as one line, Endurance gets the mile, Zimmer leaves Inspiration and Things I care about rests, and eight Inspiration cards get their lines. The footer's end credits roll and settle on the credit, the concert countdown flips down like a departure board, and the profile gets a melanoma mask that traces itself and a drone that flies its planned route. Papers that shaped me gets a line of years whose dots drop in, profile tags shared across entries light the work that uses them, the artist tiles get equalizer bars, and Interstellar gets its line.

item.title: Site changes, November 24, 2026
item.description: Books swing open to their title page, page titles ink in, brush strokes paint in on every browser, and the People I'm watching drawings play their moment. Grateful for joins the page: dusk falls as you scroll toward it, lanterns hang and sway from strings that draw themselves in, fireflies drift, stars twinkle, the moon rises, and the garden's ground runs into a night footer. Math I love frames itself, glides between steps, shows contour lines in deeper colour and can be played with. Casey Neistat becomes his vlog selfie shot. The Lord of the Rings gets its line. And stray saved-for-later text no longer shows under Independent research. Robot soccer gets a deep dive built from the case-study generator, with its drawing, share image and the report still linked, and the profile card links to it. The bike rides the footer's ridge once when you reach the bottom of a page, and wherever a link lands you glows warm for a moment. Casey Neistat joins Inspiration with a drawing of him filming himself on a board down a Manhattan avenue, map pins preview their drawing, Featured pictures tilt toward the cursor, and more icons sketch themselves in.

item.title: Site changes, November 20, 2026
item.description: Case-study results count up, the menu underline glides to the link you point at, the portrait sweeps in like a drawing, the Now dot breathes, and the Skills icons sketch in again after a typo stopped them. The story on case studies tells itself line by line, the Research and work rail fills in as you scroll, the Skills icons sketch themselves in, and Travel's colour strip fills in and lifts each trip's card. The old PortfolioWebsite link forwards to the profile, the flagship says a small network, the meta-learning at PhysicsAI was built for a fighter-jet simulation, and the mile and Ironman lose their qualifiers.

item.title: Site changes, November 19, 2026
item.description: Case studies show how far you've read and light each part's title as you reach it, the bets on Things I'm thinking about get an ink underline, and Travel's drawings develop from grey into colour. Section underlines paint themselves in, the travel map's counts climb as its pins land, and a marker slides between the Beliefs tabs. Revamping the education system is in Now, Things I'm thinking about and Things I care about, and Math I love gets the same space above it as every other section. Skills show the work that used them, book covers tilt when you point at them, the values write themselves in, and Ender's Game joins the books I've read. The travel drawings move gently, clouds drifting and bubbles rising, and a line draws down Things I'm thinking about as you read, lighting each question's number. Scuba diving is on Interests as a hobby, Sipadan and Palau so far, and on Travel as a drawn reef with a sea turtle, linked from the Sipadan pin. The math scene is linked from the profile, the papers that shaped me and Theory of AGI, each link opening its own tab. Math I love becomes one 3D scene you can turn, with a tab each for gradient descent, Lagrange multipliers, the central limit theorem, Bayesian updating and random walks. Interests gets Math I love, five small animations of ideas from probability, optimization and multivariable calculus, and an Events countdown, and a bike rides Seattle to DC as you read A hard day. The site feels live: the header says how long ago it was updated, the next trip counts down, and the map's pins drop in west to east before the routes draw. The travel map pops more, with a deeper sea, stronger green for places I've been, shadowed pins, glowing routes and a pulse on the next trips, and the Iraq route runs through Baghdad, Basra and Erbil. Travel adds the road trip across Iraq, Baghdad to Basra to Erbil, with a drawn card and a dotted route, and the footer credits drop Drawings and Tested. The site links the general resume again, with the melanoma multi-GPU work, and the Seattle to DC card on Travel links to A hard day. The footer sits centered, with its credits meeting in the middle and stacking centered on phones. The footer lines up with the narrower reading column on every page that uses it. Add How It Was Built: build history, code map and concepts, with diagrams. The site's resume becomes the Meta Simulation CV/ML version, the previous one is saved in _resumes/site-previous, and Skills adds the six skills it lists. The Seattle to DC ride links to A hard day, Writings joins the RSS feed, Dune gets a line, the profile preview is retaken, and A hard day's written and posted lines get their own colors. The opening loader takes turns through seven ink scenes (Lorenz, double pendulum, logistic map, three bodies, de Jong, a reward landscape and neural decoding), and Outside work adds leading trips to California's most intense rapids. The home page opens on the Lorenz butterfly: two paths 0.00001 apart draw as one ink line, then split. Death Valley joins the Trip timeline for November 20-22, with the Mesquite dunes, Badwater and Zabriskie Point in one drawing. IBM Research gets a drawing: contract and invoice terms matched side by side, with the mismatch flagged and the uncertain term sent to a person. IBM Research 2021 joins Research & work, the hero leads with research engineer in RL and robotics, and Avengers Assemble, four niche Methods chips and a repeated SPIE link are saved for later. The Pamir Highway in Tajikistan joins Places I'd like to go, and A hard day gets its double-rainbow photo from Medium. End credits line up with the footer's left edge.

item.title: Site changes, November 18, 2026
item.description: Grateful for fades in from the page into a dusk sky, with a cut-out crescent moon. Story spines and a storyboard on the deep dives, a color script for Travel, A113 on a Philadelphia boathouse door, end credits in every footer, and Relentless optimism joins Values. Philadelphia for Thanksgiving joins the Trip timeline with Boathouse Row at dusk, Lassen is saved for later, and the deep dives' Related work moves into the generator.

item.title: Site changes, November 16, 2026
item.description: The home page leads with the strongest work: proof-first order, two Featured projects with Replicate SOTA and Drone Autonomy in More projects, North star hidden, Papers moved to Interests, and thin projects, apps and research entries saved for later.

item.title: Site changes, November 15, 2026
item.description: Hans Zimmer joins Favorite artists. Favorite artists joins Interests, starting with Faouzia. Theory of AGI joins Thinking, Replicate SOTA's explainer goes live, the macOS note is one line, and Langer, the companies line, Products, two thin questions, the happy-to-chat line and the duplicate Recruiting entry move to comments. Kobe Bryant joins Inspiration, drawn alone in a dark gym at 4 a.m.

item.title: Site changes, November 14, 2026
item.description: Replicate SOTA takes Post Training Lab's featured spot with a deep dive and its recall chart, Post Training Lab moves to More projects, and the project share images are retaken in the new look. Warmer look with italic serif section titles and a brush stroke under each, Dune joins Want to read, a Want to learn section lists keyboard, tabla and Hindustani classical, and the half Ironman joins the races.

item.title: Site changes, November 13, 2026
item.description: AlphaGo Lite deep dive and card show generation 107 beating GNU Go's weakest level in 32 of 40 games, with the new 107-generation figure.

item.title: Site changes, November 11, 2026
item.description: Taipei joins Places I'd like to go, with Taipei 101 at dusk from Elephant Mountain and a pin on the map. Outside work drops the Tahoe relay and tightens the racing, mountains and travel lines. Outside work reads as one story: start before you're ready, then racing, then mountains, dives and Cerro Torre. Research & work gets an intro and the PhysicsAI award and fighter-jet sim, and drops the sim-limits, RLPD and EMD sentences. Outside work adds the Tahoe Marathon, SF Ultra, Death Ride and Tahoe relay, folds soccer into the track line, and trims the ski and Ironman details. Outside work adds scuba (caves, shipwrecks, 130+ feet, Africa, Palau, Monterey, Sipadan) and the cross-country ride on no prior training. Outside work adds track races, a sub-5-minute mile without training, and an Ironman on 30 training sessions. The BIDS and Perlmutter cosmology cards get drawings: particle hits in a 3D detector, and a supernova found by image subtraction.
